testCases.name: Clear ICSR with drug and adverse event
testCases.description: Article clearly describes a drug and associated adverse event - should INCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Serious hepatotoxicity associated with DrugX in clinical trial
input.articleAbstract: We report a case of severe drug-induced liver injury in a 45-year-old male patient receiving DrugX (100mg daily) for rheumatoid arthritis. The patient developed jaundice and elevated transaminases after 3 months of treatment. DrugX was discontinued and liver function normalized within 4 weeks.

expectedOutput.rationale: Article describes a serious adverse event (hepatotoxicity) associated with DrugX in a identifiable patient with temporal relationship and dechallenge positive

testCases.name: Pregnancy exposure with normal outcome
testCases.description: Pregnancy exposure registry data with normal outcome - should INCLUDE per ICH E2D

input.articleTitle: Pregnancy outcomes following DrugY exposure: a registry study
input.articleAbstract: Prospective registry of 250 pregnant women exposed to DrugY during first trimester. No increase in congenital anomalies compared to background rate. 240 live births, 5 spontaneous abortions, 5 elective terminations.

expectedOutput.rationale: Pregnancy exposure with outcome data constitutes reportable ICSR per ICH E2D and GVP Module VI regardless of outcome normality

testCases.name: Occupational exposure without adverse event
testCases.description: Occupational exposure study without reported adverse events - should EXCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Occupational exposure to DrugZ in manufacturing workers: air monitoring study
input.articleAbstract: Air monitoring in pharmaceutical manufacturing facility detected trace DrugZ levels below occupational exposure limits. No health complaints reported among 50 workers over 2-year period.

expectedOutput.rationale: Occupational exposure without any reported adverse health effect or clinical outcome does not constitute an ICSR

testCases.name: Overdose with serious outcome
testCases.description: Intentional overdose with serious clinical outcome - should INCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Fatal DrugA overdose: case report and literature review
input.articleAbstract: A 28-year-old female presented after intentional ingestion of 50 tablets of DrugA (500mg each). Developed seizures, metabolic acidosis, and multi-organ failure. Died 48 hours post-admission despite intensive care.

expectedOutput.rationale: Overdose with fatal outcome is a serious ICSR requiring expedited reporting per regulatory requirements

testCases.name: Lack of efficacy report
testCases.description: Report of suspected lack of efficacy - should INCLUDE per GVP Module VI

input.articleTitle: Treatment failure with DrugB in refractory epilepsy: case series
input.articleAbstract: Three patients with refractory epilepsy experienced breakthrough seizures after switching to generic DrugB. Seizure control restored after switching back to brand-name product. Therapeutic drug monitoring showed subtherapeutic levels with generic.

expectedOutput.rationale: Suspected lack of efficacy with clinical consequences (breakthrough seizures) is reportable per GVP Module VI

testCases.name: Medication error with harm
testCases.description: Dispensing error leading to patient harm - should INCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Dispensing error: DrugC 10mg dispensed instead of 1mg causing severe hypotension
input.articleAbstract: A 72-year-old patient received DrugC 10mg tablets instead of prescribed 1mg due to pharmacy dispensing error. Developed severe symptomatic hypotension requiring hospitalization. Recovered after 3 days.

expectedOutput.rationale: Medication error resulting in serious adverse event (hypotension requiring hospitalization) constitutes an ICSR

testCases.name: Counterfeit drug report
testCases.description: Counterfeit product identified with adverse events - should INCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Counterfeit DrugD containing toxic contaminant causes renal failure
input.articleAbstract: Investigation of counterfeit DrugD tablets found to contain diethylene glycol. Five patients developed acute renal failure after consuming counterfeit product. Two deaths reported.

expectedOutput.rationale: Counterfeit drug with serious adverse outcomes (renal failure, death) is a critical safety signal requiring immediate reporting

testCases.name: Elderly patient with drug interaction
testCases.description: Elderly patient with polypharmacy and suspected drug interaction - should INCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Warfarin-DrugE interaction causing major bleeding in elderly patient
input.articleAbstract: An 82-year-old patient on chronic warfarin therapy was prescribed DrugE for infection. INR increased from 2.5 to 8.2 within 5 days. Patient presented with gastrointestinal bleeding requiring transfusion. DrugE discontinued, INR normalized.

expectedOutput.rationale: Drug-drug interaction (Warfarin-DrugE) leading to serious hemorrhage in elderly patient with polypharmacy is a reportable ICSR

testCases.name: Pediatric exposure via breast milk
testCases.description: Infant exposure through breast milk with adverse event - should INCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Neonatal thrombocytopenia associated with maternal DrugF exposure via breast milk
input.articleAbstract: A 3-week-old exclusively breastfed infant developed severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 15,000). Mother was taking DrugF 200mg daily for autoimmune condition. Infant platelet count normalized after mother discontinued DrugF and breastfeeding paused.

expectedOutput.rationale: Adverse event in infant exposed via breast milk is reportable per ICH E2D as exposure during lactation with clinical consequence

testCases.name: Congenital anomaly report
testCases.description: Congenital anomaly following first trimester exposure - should INCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Congenital heart defect following first-trimester DrugG exposure: case report
input.articleAbstract: A newborn diagnosed with ventricular septal defect. Mother took DrugG 50mg daily during weeks 4-8 of pregnancy for chronic condition. No family history of congenital heart defects. Genetic testing negative.

expectedOutput.rationale: Congenital anomaly following first-trimester drug exposure is a serious ICSR requiring expedited reporting per regulatory requirements

testCases.name: Overdose without harm
testCases.description: Overdose case with no clinical harm - should EXCLUDE per ICH E2D

input.articleTitle: Accidental DrugH overdose in toddler: no clinical sequelae
input.articleAbstract: A 2-year-old child accidentally ingested 10 tablets of DrugH (20mg each). Emergency evaluation showed normal vital signs and laboratory values. No treatment required. Child discharged after 4-hour observation with no adverse effects.

expectedOutput.rationale: Overdose without any clinical adverse effect or medical intervention does not constitute a reportable ICSR per ICH E2D

testCases.name: Pediatric exposure with adverse event
testCases.description: Direct pediatric drug exposure with adverse event - should INCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Stevens-Johnson syndrome in child after DrugI exposure
input.articleAbstract: A 7-year-old developed Stevens-Johnson syndrome 10 days after starting DrugI for infection. Hospitalized in ICU with mucosal involvement and skin detachment affecting 15% BSA. DrugI discontinued, treated with IVIG. Slow recovery over 3 weeks.

expectedOutput.rationale: Serious adverse event (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) in pediatric patient with temporal relationship to drug exposure is a reportable ICSR

testCases.name: Elderly patient with fall after drug initiation
testCases.description: Elderly patient fall with fracture after starting new medication - should INCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Hip fracture in 85-year-old after initiating DrugJ for insomnia
input.articleAbstract: An 85-year-old nursing home resident started DrugJ 5mg nightly for insomnia. Two days later, found on floor with hip fracture. DrugJ discontinued. Surgery performed. Resident had no prior falls in 6 months.

expectedOutput.rationale: Fall with fracture in elderly patient temporally related to new sedating drug initiation constitutes suspected adverse drug reaction requiring ICSR reporting

testCases.name: Drug interaction with QT prolongation
testCases.description: Drug-drug interaction causing QT prolongation and arrhythmia - should INCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Torsades de pointes from DrugK-DrugL interaction in cardiac patient
input.articleAbstract: A 65-year-old with atrial fibrillation on DrugK (antiarrhythmic) was prescribed DrugL (antibiotic). Developed syncope. ECG showed QT prolongation (520ms) and torsades de pointes. Both drugs stopped, magnesium given, rhythm normalized.

expectedOutput.rationale: Drug-drug interaction (DrugK-DrugL) causing life-threatening arrhythmia (torsades de pointes) with QT prolongation is a serious ICSR requiring expedited reporting

testCases.name: Quality defect with microbial contamination
testCases.description: Product quality defect with microbial contamination causing infection - should INCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Bacillus cereus contamination of DrugM batches causes sepsis
input.articleAbstract: Investigation of DrugM intravenous solution found Bacillus cereus contamination in 3 production lots. Seven immunocompromised patients developed sepsis after infusion. Two deaths. Recall initiated.

expectedOutput.rationale: Product quality defect (microbial contamination) causing serious infections and deaths is a critical safety signal requiring immediate ICSR reporting and recall

testCases.name: Secondary malignancy after long-term drug use
testCases.description: Report of secondary malignancy potentially related to long-term immunosuppressant - should INCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Lymphoma after 10-year DrugN therapy for rheumatoid arthritis
input.articleAbstract: A 58-year-old patient developed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma after 10 years of continuous DrugN (TNF inhibitor) therapy for rheumatoid arthritis. No prior malignancy history. DrugN discontinued, oncology referral made.

expectedOutput.rationale: Secondary malignancy (lymphoma) after long-term immunosuppressant therapy is a serious suspected adverse reaction requiring ICSR reporting per GVP Module VI

testCases.name: Transmission via breast milk with infant adverse event
testCases.description: Drug transmitted via breast milk causing infant adverse event - should INCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Infantile spasms in breastfed infant exposed to DrugO via maternal milk
input.articleAbstract: A 2-month-old exclusively breastfed infant developed infantile spasms. Mother was taking DrugO 400mg daily for epilepsy. EEG confirmed hypsarrhythmia. Infant spasms resolved after mother switched to DrugP and breastfeeding continued.

expectedOutput.rationale: Serious neurological adverse event in infant exposed via breast milk is reportable per ICH E2D as exposure during lactation with clinical consequence requiring ICSR

testCases.name: Congenital anomaly with teratogenicity signal
testCases.description: Multiple congenital anomalies following first-trimester exposure - should INCLUDE

input.articleTitle: VACTERL association following DrugQ exposure in early pregnancy
input.articleAbstract: Newborn with VACTERL association (vertebral, anal, cardiac, tracheoesophageal, renal, limb anomalies). Mother took DrugQ 10mg daily during weeks 3-8 for chronic condition. No genetic syndrome identified. DrugQ discontinued.

expectedOutput.rationale: Multiple congenital anomalies (VACTERL association) following first-trimester drug exposure represents potential teratogenicity signal requiring expedited ICSR reporting

testCases.name: Literature review without primary case data
testCases.description: Review article without primary case reports - should EXCLUDE

input.articleTitle: Systematic review of DrugR safety profile in elderly patients
input.articleAbstract: Systematic review of 45 studies evaluating DrugR safety in patients >65 years. No new primary case reports identified. Known adverse events consistent with labeling. No new safety signals.

expectedOutput.rationale: Systematic review without primary individual case reports does not constitute an ICSR; no new identifiable case data for reporting

testCases.name: Animal study without human data
testCases.description: Preclinical animal toxicity study without human exposure - should EXCLUDE

input.articleTitle: DrugS causes hepatocellular carcinoma in rat 2-year carcinogenicity study
input.articleAbstract: Two-year carcinogenicity study in Sprague-Dawley rats showed dose-dependent increase in hepatocellular carcinoma with DrugS at 50mg/kg/day. No human exposure data. Mechanism under investigation.

expectedOutput.rationale: Preclinical animal study without any human exposure or clinical data does not constitute an ICSR; animal findings alone are not reportable as ICSRs
